- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% relative to prior peak or mean.
- After sharp spikes in price (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward — cap downward slope at 1–2% per day after peak.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates price — add 2–5% bias to forecast mean.
- If sentiment is consistently bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–3% per day.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if price is above 75% of 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture event-driven momentum — if official events are bullish, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast starting from day 10.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment swing.
